thread:
elaine_support: Customer escalation: streaming /v1/chat/stream keeps cutting out after ~15s. They see partial output then immediate client reconnects, duplicates, and billing concerns. They attached ALB access log + a node SDK trace. Can we triage? :warning:
eng-sre-bot: Assigned to infra. Please include minimal repro steps + ALB full log lines and any X-Request-Id header value.
alex_w: I'll pick this up. Quick question: what’s the exact traffic path? CF -> ALB -> nginx -> app?
elaine_support: Yes: Cloudflare (proxied DNS) -> ALB -> nginx ingress -> pod. ALB log line they sent (trimmed):
```
2026-05-03T09:12:34.567Z app-alb 10.0.0.2:443 198.51.100.22:41234 0.000 15.011 0.000 504 "GET https://api.example.com/v1/chat/stream HTTP/1.1" 502 600 0 0 "-" "Mozilla/5.0" arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:... request_id=req-xyz
```
samir_m: ALB shows a 504 in the timing with 15.011s. ALB default idle timeout is 60s, so something closed earlier (origin or proxy). We need nginx access/error logs at the same time and a tcpdump to confirm FIN/RST.
elaine_support: Customer supplied their client trace: curl -N shows chunks for 14s then connection ends. Node sdk shows ECONNRESET then immediate retry.

matt_infra: Likely culprit is an intermediate proxy closing the connection (nginx or CF). Two immediate checks for them: disable proxy buffering in nginx ingress and bypass CF to test direct-to-ALB. Also check nginx proxy_read_timeout and proxy_send_timeout.

eng-sre-bot: Triage checklist to give customer:
- full ALB access logs spanning the window
- nginx ingress access.log + error.log for the timestamp
- app logs (stdout/stderr) and any worker crashes
- curl --no-buffer -v output and node SDK trace
- tcpdump around the timeframe showing RST/FIN if possible
- include X-Request-Id in the client request so we can correlate

alex_w: Quick repro command for them to run (shows raw), and encourages HTTP/1.1 if they suspect h2 issues:
```
curl -v -N --http1.1 -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" "https://api.example.com/v1/chat/stream?debug_heartbeats=1"
```

samir_m: If they’re behind Cloudflare, note CF has its own buffering and will sometimes terminate streams if it thinks origin misbehaved. CF -> ALB HTTP/2 multiplexing can also hide origin socket events.

elaine_support: Customer provided a small tcpdump snippet from the nginx host showing a RST around 15s:
```
09:12:34.560 IP 198.51.100.22.41234 > 10.0.0.7.443: Flags [P.], seq 1:512, ack 1, win 4128
09:12:34.572 IP 10.0.0.7.443 > 198.51.100.22.41234: Flags [P.], seq 1:2048, ack 513, win 1024
09:12:49.580 IP 10.0.0.7.443 > 198.51.100.22.41234: Flags [RST, ACK]
```

matt_infra: RST at ~15s — that is consistent with an intermediate closing the socket. Possible causes: nginx hitting a buffer limit, the app process closing connection, or Cloudflare/ALB mismatch.

alex_w: For a fast test, ask them to add these nginx ingress annotations (turn off buffering and increase timeouts):
```
nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-buffering: "off"
nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-request-buffering: "off"
nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-read-timeout: "3600"
nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-send-timeout: "3600"
```
Also suggest proxy_http_version 1.1 and disable sendfile if using file descriptors.

samir_m: App-side mitigations while infra changes happen: emit a small heartbeat chunk every 10s (newline or ":\n") to keep proxies from considering the stream idle. Also make client retries back off to avoid duplicate billing; add idempotency where possible.

elaine_support: Customer asked whether we can change anything server-side. We currently send periodic heartbeats but can increase frequency for certain routes while they debug. Will need product approval for a broad change.

matt_infra: Follow-up plan: 1) customer to try bypassing CF (set DNS to gray-cloud) — if stable, CF is involved. 2) disable nginx buffering — if stable, nginx config was the issue. 3) if both still fail, capture full tcpdump and app traces.

elaine_support: Customer ran the tests and reported back: bypassing CF -> stable. Disabling nginx buffering while CF still in front -> stable. So root cause is interaction between Cloudflare buffering and nginx buffer/timeouts. They reconfigured CF origin settings (disabled response buffering) and adjusted nginx annotations and are monitoring.

eng-sre-bot: Closing the thread as resolved for now. Recommendations to include in KB: always test streaming flows by bypassing CDN first, set nginx ingress buffering off for streaming endpoints, and teach SDKs to jitter/backoff retries to reduce duplicate billing risk.

elaine_support: Thanks team. I sent the checklist and final notes to the customer; they confirmed improved stability. :white_check_mark:
